title: Playing at Audible Theatre / Minetta Lane until April 30th! #theatre ...
transcript: Hugh Jackman is back in an intimate off Broadway theatre alongside Ella Beatty in this subtly devastating play telling a fairly straightforward story of a professor having a deeply inappropriate affair with a nineteen year old student sexuaI misconduct of the middle classes is deceptively simple in some ways; it takes us through the beats of this ordeal from beginning to end in pretty much the way you'd expect at first but almost like in a Greek tragedy the playwright Hannah Moscovitch embraces that sense of inevitability the looming dread of knowing where this is headed but in a way that adds to the tension rather than deflates it if there is an enigma that keeps us on her hook it's the question of why she chose to tell this story not only from the professor's perspective but narrated in third person but by the end she answers this question pretty definitively with a meta theatrical flourish while still leaving some room for our subjective reactions and judgments And regardless of whether the play surprises or challenges us it still hits like a ton of bricks when the consequences come rearing their head there's a moment maybe halfway through the play when the affair is like “going well” so far but he gives her some positive feedback on her writing and she just burst into tears with her head buried in her hands and it so succinctly conveys just how devastatingly important this man's validation is to her we get a few more of these moments where her ostensibly enthusiastic consent begins to show its cracks not through defiant soapboxing but sometimes just with a few sharp probing questions that she manages to voice in the midst of her uncertainty so while the subject matter is definitely rough I found myself pretty moved by it and also just gripped from beginning to end
reasoning: Reviewer describes the play as subtly devastating, praises the writing and performances, and says they were moved and gripped from beginning to end.
